# 8. Control index

<!-- generated by tools/render_docs.py - do not edit by hand -->

ESMA GL4 para 51 is the obligation: firms should view the information collected as a whole, be alert to relevant contradictions, and contact the client to resolve material inconsistencies. GL4 para 49 describes the mechanism: risk-profiling software "could include some controls of coherence of the replies provided by clients in order to highlight contradictions between different pieces of information collected". These are those controls.

Severity:

| | |
|---|---|
| `block` | No recommendation may be produced until the issue is resolved |
| `refer` | The recommendation is withheld pending an adviser conversation with the client, which is documented |
| `cap`   | The profile is capped automatically and the client is told |
| `note`  | Recorded on file, no automatic effect |

Every control is one-way: it can hold a profile where it is or move it down. None can move it up.

| id | severity | control | condition | effect | basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CC01` | `cap` | Knowledge over-estimation | `self_rating >= 4 and comprehension_correct <= 3` | knowledge band capped at the comprehension ceiling | ESMA GL4 paras 46, 52 |
| `CC02` | `refer` | Low knowledge with high risk appetite | `knowledge_band <= 2 and tolerance_band >= 4` | recommendation withheld pending adviser discussion and re-confirmation | ESMA GL4 para 51 (explicit example: little knowledge, aggressive risk attitude) |
| `CC03` | `refer` | Tolerance materially exceeds capacity | `tolerance_band - capacity_band >= 2` | capacity governs; the gap is explained to the client and recorded | MiFID II Art. 25(2); ESMA GL4 para 51 |
| `CC04` | `cap` | Stated loss tolerance exceeds absorbable loss | `tolerance_loss_pct > capacity_loss_pct` | risk band capped at the highest band whose stress loss <= capacity_loss_pct | MiFID II Art. 25(2) - ability to bear losses |
| `CC05` | `cap` | Horizon inconsistent with objective | `objective_band >= 4 and horizon_band <= 2` | horizon governs; long-term objective cannot be pursued over a short horizon | DR 2017/565 Art. 54(5) |
| `CC06` | `cap` | Liquidity need inside the horizon | `C8 in ['small_early','large_early'] and horizon_band >= 3` | effective horizon reduced to the earliest expected withdrawal | ESMA GL3 para 37; GL8 para 80 |
| `CC07` | `refer` | Return expectation not achievable at the accepted risk level | `expectation_band - final_band >= 2` | risk/return relationship re-explained and the answer re-taken | ESMA GL2 para 23; GL4 para 51 |
| `CC08` | `cap` | No emergency reserve | `C7 == 'm_0'` | capacity band capped at 2 | ESMA GL8 para 80 - client must be able to finance the investment |
| `CC09` | `cap` | Concentration in a single mandate | `invested_share_of_financial_assets > 0.50` | risk band capped per the concentration overlay | ESMA GL8 para 89 |
| `CC10` | `block` | Borrowing to invest | `C10 == true` | no recommendation under this framework | ESMA GL8 para 80; GL3 para 36 |
| `CC11` | `cap` | Vulnerability overlay | `any of A7 in ['sole_income_source','first_time_investor'] or age >= 75` | risk band capped at 3 unless the adviser documents a reasoned override | ESMA GL3 para 40 |
| `CC12` | `refer` | Profile upgraded immediately before a recommendation | `profile_updated_within_days <= 5 and final_band increased vs previous` | flagged to compliance; rationale for the change must be recorded | ESMA GL5 para 58 |
| `CC13` | `block` | Incomplete necessary information | `any required question in the applicable set is unanswered` | no investment service or financial instrument may be recommended | DR 2017/565 Art. 54(8) |
| `CC14` | `cap` | Divergent profiles within a group | `A2 in ['joint_group','represented'] and band spread across persons >= 2` | the most prudent profile governs (least knowledgeable, weakest financial situation, most conservative objectives). Profiles are never averaged. | ESMA GL6 paras 69-70 |

## Client-facing wording

What the suitability report says to the client when each control fires.

**CC01 — Knowledge over-estimation**

> Your answers to the worked examples suggest a different level of familiarity from the one you selected. We have used the worked examples.

**CC02 — Low knowledge with high risk appetite**

> You told us you are comfortable with a high level of risk, but your answers to the worked examples suggest the risks involved may not yet be familiar. We want to talk this through with you before recommending anything.

**CC03 — Tolerance materially exceeds capacity**

> What you are willing to risk and what your finances can absorb are two different things, and here they are some way apart. We have to work to the lower of the two.

**CC04 — Stated loss tolerance exceeds absorbable loss**

> The loss you told us you would accept is larger than the loss you told us you could absorb without changing your plans. We have used the amount you could absorb.

**CC05 — Horizon inconsistent with objective**

> The objective you chose normally needs a longer holding period than the one you gave us. We have used your holding period.

**CC06 — Liquidity need inside the horizon**

> You expect to need some of this money within the first two years, so we have treated this as a short-term investment even though you gave a longer horizon.

**CC07 — Return expectation not achievable at the accepted risk level**

> The return you are expecting is higher than the level of risk you have accepted can reasonably deliver. We would like to go through the relationship between the two with you again.

**CC08 — No emergency reserve**

> You have no cash set aside outside this investment. We think a reserve should come first, and we have limited the level of risk accordingly.

**CC09 — Concentration in a single mandate**

> This investment is a large share of your financial assets. Concentrating that much in one strategy adds risk that is separate from the strategy itself, so we have limited the level of risk.

**CC10 — Borrowing to invest**

> We cannot advise on an investment funded by borrowing or by pledging other assets.

**CC11 — Vulnerability overlay**

> Because of your circumstances we have taken a more cautious approach than your answers alone would suggest.

**CC12 — Profile upgraded immediately before a recommendation**

> Your profile changed shortly before this recommendation. We record why, so that neither of us is relying on a change made for the wrong reason.

**CC13 — Incomplete necessary information**

> We are missing information we need. Until we have it we are not permitted to recommend any investment service or financial instrument to you.

**CC14 — Divergent profiles within a group**

> Your answers differ from each other in ways that matter. We have used the more cautious of the two throughout, rather than splitting the difference.

## Where the conditions live

The severity, regulatory basis, stated effect and client wording of every control are configuration, in `config/scoring.yaml`. The **conditions** are implemented in code, in `src/suitability/consistency.py`, and not evaluated from strings: a suitability control that can be switched off by editing a text expression is not a control. `tests/test_consistency.py::test_every_configured_control_is_implemented` keeps the two lists in step, and there is one test per control.
